L-r1-01: Control. Clean, but the name is small and light for busy wood; no link to the app icon.
L-r1-02: The cream tile ties the bar to the app icon at once. Tile is the brightest thing on the bar.
L-r1-03: Bold 700 reads better on wood than 600; 28 tile matches the cap height. Kept for round 2.
L-r1-04: Burned mark is on theme (branded into the board). Dark square can read as a hole. Kept.
L-r1-05: Cut: bare 'sc' + 'SupperCraft' reads as the name twice.
L-r1-06: Cut: the gold coin reads as a badge or prize; gold is not in the palette.
L-r1-07: Patch was drawn in the wrong place (status bar). Fixed and retried in round 2.
L-r1-08: Cut: the two weights are too close to see, and 500 looks thin on wood.
L-r1-09: Condensed Plex is taller and stamped, still the app font. Kept.
L-r1-10: Warmest, most crafted. But serif breaks DESIGN 2.5.5 (Garamond was removed on purpose). Kept as the exception lane.
L-r1-11: Cut: upright Garamond looks like a book cover, not a kitchen tool.
L-r1-12: Georgia Bold Italic (free twin: Gelasio) is warm and sturdy. Serif exception lane.
L-r1-13: Cut: Palatino at this size is thin and bookish; the outline mark looks like a button.
L-r1-14: Cut: the 'Tyler' chip is heavy and duplicates the avatar menu; the shadow is decorative (2.8.4).
L-r1-15: Cut: search, + and bell crowd the bar; + doubles Capture; search is ruled out (4.1.2).
L-r1-16: Cut: the page name repeats the page title below and was taken out on purpose (D7 A).
L-r1-17: 64 is good on a computer but eats 14 more points of every phone screen. Height lesson only.
L-r1-18: 44 is cramped: the tile shrinks to 22 and the avatar touches the edges.
L-r1-19: The bottom edge makes the bar feel like a real board with a lip. Kept.
L-r1-20: Cut: the household line fails contrast (4.4:1) and crowds the name.
L-r2-01: Clean and clear. Bold reads on any block. The edge gives the bar a real lip.
L-r2-02: Burned mark fits the wood story, but at 28 it is dim and looks like a hole.
L-r2-03: Maple inlay mark: a lighter wood set into the board. Calmer than the cream tile, still on theme.
L-r2-04: Condensed Plex: taller letters, stamped feel, still the app font.
L-r2-05: Cut: the dark patch shows hard edges and looks like a smudge on the board.
L-r2-06: Cut: the plank looks like a big button, and adds a box to the bar.
L-r2-07: Bug: the avatar did not draw (only the chevron). Fixed and retried as L-r3-04.
L-r2-08: Georgia Bold Italic: warmest name yet. Needs a serif exception (2.5.5) and the free twin Gelasio.
L-r2-09: Cut: Garamond's curly 'ft' looks fancy, less kitchen, and Garamond was removed on purpose.
L-r2-10: Near r2-01; 650 at 94% width is a hair softer. Merged into r3-01 (kept the 32 avatar).
L-r2-11: 52 works but the 44 targets get only 4 points above and below. Kept as the low-height option.
L-r2-12: Lit status slot fits fine. The answer to 'what else': only live status, never buttons.
L-r3-01: Best Plex version. Only question left: the edge shadow (nice lip, but 2.8.4 bans decorative shadows).
L-r3-02: Maple inlay with regular Plex: good, but the tan mark and cream name fight a little.
L-r3-03: Condensed Plex + maple inlay: the most crafted look in the app font.
L-r3-04: Chevron says 'menu', but most apps manage without it; one more small thing to read.
L-r3-05: Serif lane best: warm and sturdy. Fit stays 5 until Tyler rules the wordmark is a logo.
L-r3-06: Cut: the sheen darkens the board's bottom and the tile shadow is decorative.
L-r3-07: 52 is fine; 56 reads calmer and gives 6 points around the 44 targets. Fallback height.
L-r3-08: Shallower burn reads as a brand, not a hole. Dimmer than the tile; an option if the cream tile feels too bright.
L-r3-09: The busiest state (saving + timer) still fits at 390 wide. The right side needs nothing more.
L-r3-10: Pick: cleanest, all in the app's own kit, rule-safe edge.
